text:
Situation: As of 2026-10-21, rocuronium bromide remains on the FDA drug shortage list. Corvale East holds 7.1 days of 10 mg/mL 5 mL vials across presentations. Corvale Lakeside holds 28.5 days and Corvale General holds 19.2 days of comparable supply.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the rocuronium bromide shortage on 2023-02-15 and lists multiple manufacturers as Current, including Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Inc. and Hospira, Inc. The Hikma product used at Corvale sites is manufactured at HIKMA FARMACEUTICA (PORTUGAL), S.A. (FEI 3002807173), a registered plant whose last inspection was VAI on 2023-04-21. That plant received a VAI classification on 2023-02-03, which was 12 days before FDA posted the shortage on 2023-02-15. An earlier inspection of the same plant ended 2020-03-06 with a VAI classification, 1076 days before the posting. Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1021343) is an approved alternate manufacturer with a registered plant last inspected NAI on 2025-02-07.

Our position: Supply at Corvale East is below the two-week target. Corvale Lakeside and Corvale General have sufficient inventory to support limited transfers while maintaining their own two-week buffers. Hospira product is an approved alternate with recent NAI inspection.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 13 vials of 10 mg/mL 5 mL from Corvale Lakeside to Corvale East — approved by Pharmacy Director (transfer request).
2. Transfer 40 vials of 10 mg/mL 5 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — approved by Pharmacy Director (transfer request).
3. Procure Hospira rocuronium bromide 10 mg/mL as alternate manufacturer — approved by Pharmacist verification.
4. Evaluate purchase from B. Braun Medical Inc. — approved by Buyer.
5. Evaluate purchase from BE Pharmaceuticals Inc. — approved by Buyer.

Not recommended: No clinical dosing changes or protocol modifications; those are for treating clinicians and the committee.
